## Findings
- claim-1: Let \(N\ge0\), \(R:\mathbb Z^s\to\mathbb Z^m\), and \(Q=\operatorname{coker}R\). Put \(t=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}R\). Smith normal form gives \(U\in\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbb Z)\), \(V\in\mathrm{GL}_s(\mathbb Z)\), with \(\det U,\det V=\pm1\), such that \[ URV=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_t,0,\ldots,0),\qquad 1\le d_1\mid\cdots\mid d_t . \] Therefore \[ Q\cong\bigoplus_{\nu=1}^{t}\mathbb Z/d_\nu\mathbb Z\ \oplus\ \mathbb Z^{m-t}. \] Hence \[ Q\cong\mathbb Z^N \iff t=m-N\ \text{and}\ d_\nu=1\ (1\le\nu\le t). \] Indeed, under these conditions \(\mathbb Z/d_\nu\mathbb Z=0\), giving \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^{m-t}=\mathbb Z^N\). Conversely, a factor \(d_\nu>1\) supplies nonzero torsion, impossible in \(\mathbb Z^N\), and the free rank is \(m-t=N\). Boundary cases are included: if \(t=0\), the invariant-factor condition is vacuous and \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^m\); if \(m=0\), then \(Q=0=\mathbb Z^0\); if \(N=0\), the criterion requires \(t=m\) and all \(d_\nu=1\), equivalently \(Q=0\).
- claim-2: With \(q=n-r\), the source identifies \(A:=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) as a quotient whose surviving Schur classes are those indexed by \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\), and states that \[ J_v\subseteq A \quad\text{is generated as an ideal by}\quad \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r\}. \] [source-2@L1310-L1324|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: Assume \(1\le i\le q\), \(1\le j\le r\), set \(d_0=ij\), \(D=rq\), and define, for each integer \(d\), \[ B_d:=\{\lambda:\ i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r,\ |\lambda|=d\}, \qquad m_d:=|B_d|. \] The degree-\(d\) part of \(J_v\) is \[ (J_v)_d=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in B_d}\mathbb Zs_\lambda. \] Explicitly, the displayed generators give the inclusion from right to left. Conversely, the Littlewood--Richardson expansion \[ s_\alpha s_\mu=\sum_{\lambda}c_{\alpha\mu}^{\lambda}s_\lambda \] has \(c_{\alpha\mu}^{\lambda}=0\) unless \(\mu\subseteq\lambda\); thus multiplication of a class containing \(i^j\) produces only classes containing \(i^j\), with classes outside \(q^r\) zero in \(A\). The Schur classes in \(q^r\) are linearly independent, so the sum is direct. Let \[ T_d:=\{(k,\alpha,\mu):1\le k\le d-d_0,\ \alpha\subseteq q^r,\ |\alpha|=k,\ \mu\in B_{d-k}\}, \qquad s_d:=|T_d|. \] Define the integer matrix \[ R_d:\mathbb Z^{s_d}\longrightarrow\mathbb Z^{m_d} \] using the bases \(T_d\) and \(B_d\), respectively, by \[ (R_d)_{\lambda,(k,\alpha,\mu)}=c_{\alpha\mu}^{\lambda} \qquad(\lambda\in B_d). \] Thus its column indexed by \((k,\alpha,\mu)\) is the Schur-coordinate vector of \(s_\alpha s_\mu\). Since the image of \(\Lambda_+\) in \(A\) is \(A_+\), \[ (\Lambda_+J_v)_d=(A_+J_v)_d=\operatorname{im}R_d, \qquad (J_v/\Lambda_+J_v)_d\cong\operatorname{coker}R_d. \] Consequently, for prescribed \(N_d\ge0\), \[ (J_v/\Lambda_+J_v)_d\cong\mathbb Z^{N_d} \iff \operatorname{rank}R_d=m_d-N_d \ \text{and every nonzero Smith factor of }R_d\text{ is }1. \] For \(d<d_0\) or \(d>D\), \(B_d=T_d=\varnothing\), so \(m_d=s_d=0\), \(R_d:0\to0\), and the quotient degree is \(0\). At \(d=d_0\), \(B_{d_0}=\{i^j\}\), \(T_{d_0}=\varnothing\), and \(R_{d_0}:0\to\mathbb Z\), so the quotient degree is canonically \(\mathbb Z[s_{i^j}]\). Globally, with \[ R:=\bigoplus_{d=d_0}^{D}R_d,\qquad m:=\sum_{d=d_0}^{D}m_d,\qquad N:=\sum_{d=d_0}^{D}N_d, \] one has \[ J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\operatorname{coker}R. \] Thus the preceding rank-plus-Smith criterion applies to this finite block-diagonal presentation. No ranks or Smith factors for general parameters are asserted here.
## Strategy
Let \(N\ge0\) and \(R:\mathbb Z^s\to\mathbb Z^m\). Put \(t=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}R\). Smith normal form gives unimodular matrices
\[
U\in\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbb Z),\qquad V\in\mathrm{GL}_s(\mathbb Z),
\qquad \det U,\det V\in\{\pm1\},
\]
such that
\[
URV=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_t,0,\ldots,0),
\quad 1\le d_1\mid\cdots\mid d_t.
\]
Hence
\[
\operatorname{coker}R\cong
\bigoplus_{\nu=1}^{t}\mathbb Z/d_\nu\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z^{m-t}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\operatorname{coker}R\cong\mathbb Z^N
\iff
t=m-N\ \text{and}\ d_\nu=1\ (1\le\nu\le t).
\]
Indeed, the displayed conditions make every finite cyclic factor zero and leave free rank \(m-t=N\). Conversely, \(\mathbb Z^N\) is torsion-free, so each \(d_\nu=1\), and its rank forces \(m-t=N\).

Boundary cases are included: if \(t=0\), the invariant-factor condition is vacuous and the cokernel is \(\mathbb Z^m\); if \(s=0\), this is the same case; if \(m=0\), the cokernel is \(0\) and the criterion forces \(N=0\); if \(N=0\), it requires \(t=m\) and all \(d_\nu=1\).

For \(Q=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\), set \(q=n-r\), \(d_0=ij\), and \(D=rq\). For \(d_0\le d\le D\), define
\[
B_d=\{\lambda:i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r,\ |\lambda|=d\},
\qquad m_d=|B_d|,
\]
and
\[
T_d=\{(k,\alpha,\mu):1\le k\le d-d_0,\ 
\alpha\subseteq q^r,\ |\alpha|=k,\ \mu\in B_{d-k}\},
\qquad s_d=|T_d|.
\]
Using the Schur bases indexed by \(T_d\) and \(B_d\), respectively, define
\[
R_d:\mathbb Z^{s_d}\longrightarrow\mathbb Z^{m_d},
\qquad
(R_d)_{\lambda,(k,\alpha,\mu)}=c_{\alpha\mu}^{\lambda},
\]
where \(c_{\alpha\mu}^{\lambda}\) is the Littlewood--Richardson coefficient.

The source-backed ideal description and the LR containment condition imply
\[
(J_v)_d=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in B_d}\mathbb Zs_\lambda,
\qquad
(\Lambda_+J_v)_d=(A_+J_v)_d=\operatorname{im}R_d.
\]
Thus
\[
Q_d\cong\operatorname{coker}R_d,
\]
and, for prescribed target ranks \(N_d\ge0\),
\[
Q_d\cong\mathbb Z^{N_d}
\iff
\operatorname{rank}R_d=m_d-N_d
\ \text{and every nonzero Smith factor of }R_d\text{ is }1.
\]
Here \(m=m_d\), \(N=N_d\), and \(R=R_d\) degreewise.

At \(d=d_0\), \(B_{d_0}=\{i^j\}\), \(T_{d_0}=\varnothing\), and
\[
R_{d_0}:0\to\mathbb Z,\qquad Q_{d_0}\cong\mathbb Z[s_{i^j}].
\]
For \(d<d_0\) or \(d>D\), \(J_{v,d}=0\), hence \(Q_d=0\). In particular, no assertion is made that \(T_d\) is empty for \(d>D\): under the displayed formula it can be nonempty, but its associated map has zero codomain and cokernel \(0\).

Finally,
\[
R=\bigoplus_{d=d_0}^{D}R_d,\qquad
Q\cong\operatorname{coker}R,
\]
is a finite block-diagonal presentation. If all prescribed degreewise conditions hold, then \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^{\sum_dN_d}\).

## Gaps
No ranks, Smith invariant factors, or target values \(N_d\) are computed for general parameters. The certificate does not establish any parent freeness or minimality statement.
